note: Rejudged after 1dbfd1d7b7 changed Negotiate to record the peer's Multiprotocol order and Families to answer it. Draft Section 4: "The Software Version Capability MUST only be used for displaying the version of a BGP speaker's router daemon to make troubleshooting easier." Producers at HEAD conform: parseCapability keeps code 75 as an opaque Unknown, Negotiate's remote loop only marks peerCodes for it, and remoteOrder takes Multiprotocol entries alone, so code 75 cannot reach the family order. The positive is sound: exact Unknown code and bytes, and PeerAdvertised(75). The negative is weak: it claims an OPEN with code 75 negotiates exactly what the same OPEN without it does, yet compares a field subset. Families() now has a session-visible order (negotiated event, ADD-PATH lists, ExaBGP bridge) and the test compares it with ElementsMatch, a multiset check; Encoding.Families is re-sorted in buildSubComponents, so no assertion sees that order. Session.LinkLocalNextHop, Session.HoldTime and Identity are not compared either. A break that lets code 75 reorder Families() or set LinkLocalNextHop or HoldTime leaves the test green, which breaks the 'decides nothing' claim. The recorded discrimination breaks replace all of Negotiate with a panic, so they show the units call Negotiate, not that they catch code 75 changing a decision. Fix: in TestSoftwareVersionCapabilityDecidesNothing, assert.Equal on Families() (order-sensitive) and on Session and Identity, or compare the whole Negotiated with peerCodes cleared; put the code-75 Unknown between the two Multiprotocol entries in softverSessionCaps so a position-sensitive break shows; record a discrimination break that makes code 75 change negotiated state (e.g. reorder families) rather than panicking Negotiate.
